markdown_report:
**Recommendation: validate the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter with bounded, reversible faults before adding further probes.** At 20% progress, this remains feasible preparation for training experiments; it offers no demonstrated HR@10 improvement.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Sampled training pairwise accuracy is 96.64–99.33%, establishing fitted-pair separation without held-out evidence. (2) Endpoint effective ranks span 18.21–29.22, describing variation rather than relevance. (3) Local-signal measurements are unavailable and category identities are unknown in candidate-depth reports; explicit contracts should precede interpretation.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet’s residual causal convolutions specify temporal invariance [1]. Independently implemented assertions can test it. (2) Recommender metamorphic testing supports relational checks [2]; the cited mutation study concerns industrial optimisation, providing transferable methodology rather than recommendation evidence [3]. (3) Activation-patching outcomes depend on interventions and metrics [4], motivating sham and restoration controls. (4) Hypergeometric sampling supplies an analytical candidate-rank oracle [5], but sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model comparisons [6].

The research directions remain interface integrity, diagnostic sensitivity, and temporal dependence:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Gap | Proposed measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Interface integrity | Identity/batch checks pass | Routing and readout coverage | Explicit category and independent readout controls |
| Diagnostic sensitivity | Numerous descriptive probes | Unknown fault detection | Reversible mutations and analytical rank checks |
| Temporal dependence | Perturbation machinery | Omitted paired outcomes | Fixed-candidate rank and causal-feature contrasts |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Explicit category/scorer contract | 2/6/2 | Clarifies unsupported analyses | Primarily integration |
| **Reversible fault calibration** [2,3,5] | **4/7/6** | Tests diagnostics without retraining | Synthetic coverage limits transfer |
| Paired block restoration [1,4] | 5/7/6 | Localizes network dependence | Corruption complicates interpretation |

The selected algorithm freezes training-prefix examples, candidates, specification-derived oracles, tolerances, and operators before inspection. It temporarily introduces incorrect count-minus-one readout, genuine future-embedding dependence, or residual-branch suppression. Positive score scaling supplies ranking invariance; clean reruns and restoration supply controls. Future injection must use the current forward’s changed future embedding and add to existing residual output.

Independently verify final-nonpadding indices, causal prefix invariance, and residual `x+F(x)`. Check frozen-score nested ranks against exact eligible-pool ranks and hypergeometric expectations. Report readout disagreement, future-feature sensitivity, rank invariance, restoration errors, fault outcomes, and clean false alarms. An unchanged suppressed branch is ineffective on exercised inputs, not proven equivalent. Report unresolved equivalence explicitly; do not remove surviving faults post hoc to improve detection rates.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe`, `run_full_diagnosis`, the interpretation-prompt function, and every ModelView interface. Use deterministic histories or previously cached cloned batches without advancing the training loader. Restore hooks, individual module modes, cloned buffers, and relevant RNG states in `finally`; abort subsequent training if restoration fails.

Prevent diagnostic shortcut learning by freezing independent oracles and reserving entire operator families for later evaluation where feasible. All ranks remain in-sample; uncertainty excludes training-seed and adaptive-search effects. Keep one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, unchanged production inference, and selection solely through pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

idea.description: Calibrate the existing NextItNet diagnostic adapter using specification-derived reference checks, a bounded panel of reversible faults, and analytical candidate-sampling controls on fixed training examples. Fit no additional predictor and leave production inference unchanged.
idea.motivation: Strong sampled training separation and varied representations do not establish that diagnostics detect implementation faults or explain recommendation failures. The earlier proposal also understated implementation difficulty and misidentified an industrial optimisation mutation study as recommender research. Independently frozen oracles and explicit restoration checks make the audit more defensible, while preserving its limited claim: synthetic diagnostic validity rather than improved recommendation quality.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch, and all ModelView interfaces. view.model remains the actual trained NextItNet nn.Module; retain item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Require an explicit host-supplied category identity for named reports. Unknown identity or unsupported scorer/objective contracts produce null results with reasons, rather than inferred routes or objectives.

Freeze the protocol before observing mutant results. Select up to 32 identified training users/category using a private seed-42 generator after deterministic mapped-ID sorting. Use each eligible user's last training interaction as target and preceding history as prefix, applying baseline truncation and left padding. Record original and retained lengths, repeated targets, eligibility, exclusions, exact candidate IDs and skipped counts. Keep the baseline candidate policy explicit. Do not silently conflate the training-observed candidate-depth pool with the baseline sampler's vocabulary support. Require nonempty prefixes and report coverage of different padding lengths. Training targets may have influenced fitting; their ranks are in-sample diagnostics.

Construct this panel directly from permitted deterministic histories, or consume previously cached cloned batches supplied by the host. Retain the train_loader argument for compatibility but do not create or advance its iterator for this suite: main-process RNG restoration cannot rewind worker processes, sampler progress or prefetch queues. Use only public histories and available titles, descriptions and timestamps. Ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility and simulator traits remain unavailable unless directly evidenced by permitted text; do not infer latent intent from perturbation responses.

Define independent oracles as specification-derived assertions or separately implemented references, frozen before tuning the probes. Compute reference readout indices by independently enumerating nonpadding positions. The clean readout uses the largest nonzero index, never count-1. The incorrect count-minus-one gather exists only in the diagnostic mutation. Separately report differing indices, differing selected features, score changes and oracle detections; an incorrect index can select a coincidentally identical feature.

For causality, choose valid positions t<j and create paired inputs whose prefix through t is identical and whose future nonpadding token at j differs. Compare all features through t in evaluation mode. The positive-control mutation must capture the current forward's embedding at j and add a declared scaled copy to the hooked output at t. Use the same injection rule for both paired forwards, so the injected contribution actually depends on the changed future input. A constant offset cannot validate future-dependence detection. Specify the exact embedding boundary, hook boundary, positions, donor-token selection and amplitudes in trial-local metadata. A suggested frozen amplitude grid is 0.01, 0.1 and 1.0; document representation scale. This tests the exercised boundary, not every possible causal pathway.

For recognized residual blocks, independently compare the output against x+F(x), reproducing actual normalization, masking and dropout-disabled evaluation semantics. Temporary branch suppression changes the mapping to x and must preserve surrounding masks. Future injection adds to the existing residual output rather than replacing it with F(x). If the graph cannot be reproduced safely, return null. Suppression can be behaviorally ineffective when F(x)=0 or changes do not reach measured outputs; neither outcome proves semantic equivalence or that retraining without the branch would preserve accuracy. Include identity patches and matched unrelated-donor sham patches when exercising activation restoration; their effect has no universal desirable direction.

Use module-local forward hooks. Clone captured observations and clone outputs before modification, returning modified clones. Track only newly installed handles and remove each in nested try/finally even when forward raises; preserve pre-existing hooks. Snapshot every module's training flag individually and clone all registered buffers, including nonpersistent buffers, preserving None values and alias relationships where applicable. Restore under no_grad and restore individual flags without recursive train() calls that overwrite mixed modes. Do not use a shallow state_dict snapshot. Run without gradients and never change parameter values, optimizer state, checkpoints or production routes. Preserve Python and NumPy RNG state and use torch.random.fork_rng for CPU and relevant CUDA devices; snapshot any separate generators actually used by the suite. Local generators must not alter training generators. Verify clean feature and score restoration after each mutation and final cleanup. Restoration failure invalidates the audit and must stop subsequent training until the failure is resolved.

Freeze numerical criteria before inspecting results. Use atol=1e-6 and rtol=1e-5 for feature/score equality in the declared precision; report maximum absolute differences and nonfinite outputs. Record precision, software versions, device and deterministic settings. Positive frozen-score scaling by 2 must preserve total-order ranks, using score descending and ascending item ID for ties. Nonfinite or overflowed outputs invalidate that instance rather than becoming invariance failures. Raw margins may change. Repeat unchanged-model forwards to measure clean-control alarms; report counts and denominators rather than claiming population specificity from a small deterministic panel.

Calibrate candidate-depth calculations independently of neural forwards using frozen finite scores. For each user's actual eligible negative pool of size N, let K count negatives preceding the positive under the fixed total order. Draw unique uniform negatives from private random permutations and use nested prefixes. For m negatives, sampled rank is 1+X with X~Hypergeom(N,K,m); its expectation is 1+mK/N and its HR@10 expectation is hypergeom.cdf(9,N,K,m). For N>1, rank variance is m(K/N)(1-K/N)(N-m)/(N-1); handle N=0 and N=1 directly. Nested rank cannot decrease and hit cannot increase; m=N must reproduce exact rank and hit. Use m in {99,499,999,N} only when valid, deduplicating depths and recording unavailable ones. Existing exact-rank subsets can be reused when their eligibility and total order match; otherwise bound exact scoring to at most eight selected users/category, streaming chunks of at most 4096. Use 200 private permutations for this CPU-side check. Report observed means, analytical expectations and Monte Carlo uncertainty; at p=0 or p=1, the expected hit is deterministic. Do not turn ordinary stochastic deviations into faults without a predeclared simultaneous error policy. Agreement validates sampling arithmetic, not full-catalog model ordering or held-out relevance.

Report fault outcomes by operator, severity and input: invalid, applicable, activated, behaviorally effective, ineffective on exercised inputs, detected, independently proven equivalent, known non-equivalent and unresolved. A mutant is equivalent only if it preserves specified observables for all admissible inputs; unchanged sampled HR or survival is insufficient. Define the mutation score as killed eligible known non-equivalent mutants divided by all eligible known non-equivalent mutants, using exclusions frozen independently of outcomes. Do not exclude a known non-equivalent surviving mutant merely because the panel failed to activate it; report activation and conditional detection separately. Unresolved equivalence stays outside that score with its count visible. Behavioral effectiveness must use observables defined independently of the detector under evaluation, avoiding circular eligibility.

Prevent diagnostic overfitting by freezing assertions and tolerances before fault runs and avoiding detector changes made to kill inspected mutants. If the suite is developed adaptively, reserve entire fault-generation families for later assessment; new examples of an already inspected operator are not held-out families. With few operator families, report the resulting coverage limit rather than implying broad generalization. The audit does not explain broad-relatedness errors, quantify human intent, or establish that any training intervention will help. Retain paired temporal-rank measurements as a later research direction, and keep qualitative feedback separate from fixed validation selection.

Record synchronized GPU runtime, CPU sampling runtime, forward/scoring counts, artifacts, all protocol choices and configuration attempts beneath the current trial directory. Preserve the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget, Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], supplied splits and pinned evaluator. Each category loads exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint. No additional model, checkpoint averaging, score fusion, external data, other-trial artifacts or hidden-test access is introduced. Training and production predictor architecture remain unchanged; any later architecture intervention must update the predictor writer consistently. Subsequent selection uses only the host's unchanged macro validation HR@10. No validation interface is assumed available to this diagnostic adapter.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    retain existing bounded metrics and definitions
    protocol = frozen_oracles_operators_tolerances_and_reporting_rules()
    panel = deterministic_training_histories_or_cached_cloned_batches(cap=32)
    # Do not instantiate or advance the training loader iterator.
    snapshot = save_individual_modes_cloned_buffers_and_rng_states()
    temporary_handles = []
    try:
        set_actual_nextitnet_to_eval()
        freeze_category_candidates_exclusions_and_total_order(panel)
        clean = evaluate_with_largest_nonzero_readout(panel)
        check_independent_readout_causality_and_residual_references(clean)
        measure_clean_rerun_false_alarms(panel)
        verify_positive_finite_score_scaling_preserves_ranks(clean, factor=2)
        for operator, severity in protocol.mutations:
            classify_applicability_without_using_detector_outcomes()
            try:
                install_local_hooks_with_cloned_outputs(operator, severity)
                if operator_is_future_injection:
                    # Each paired forward captures its own future embedding.
                    mutated = evaluate_prefix_identical_future_different_pair(panel)
                else:
                    mutated = evaluate_same_panel(panel)
                record_activation_effect_and_independent_oracle_detection(mutated)
            finally:
                remove_only_this_suite_temporary_hooks()
                restore_cloned_buffers_individual_modes_and_relevant_rng_states()
            verify_clean_output_restoration_or_invalidate_and_stop()
        for user in bounded_exact_rank_subset(cap=8):
            scores, N, K = stream_frozen_eligible_pool_scores(user, chunk=4096)
            for permutation in private_uniform_permutations(count=200):
                ranks = rank_nested_prefixes_at_valid_depths(permutation)
                assert_nested_rank_and_hit_relations(ranks)
                assert_full_pool_endpoint_matches_exact_rank(ranks)
            compare_rank_and_hit_summaries_with_hypergeometric_expectations(N, K)
        report_operator_outcomes_and_frozen_denominator_mutation_score()
        report_control_alarms_uncertainty_missingness_and_runtime()
    finally:
        remove_all_remaining_suite_handles()
        restore_all_cloned_buffers_individual_modes_and_rng_states(snapshot)
    verify_final_clean_restoration_or_invalidate_and_stop()
    return {'metrics': measured_results,
            'metric_definitions': frozen_definitions_populations_and_limitations}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, denominators and unavailable fields
    distinguish activation, behavioral effect, detection and proven equivalence
    distinguish analytical sampling correctness from full-catalog model ordering
    distinguish in-sample audit ranks from pinned validation HR@10
    identify synthetic coverage and diagnostic-overfitting limitations
    prohibit unsupported intent, compatibility and performance claims

originality.positive: Combines NextItNet-specific reversible faults, independent structural assertions and analytical candidate-rank controls within one bounded diagnostic adapter.
originality.negative: Metamorphic testing, mutation analysis and hypergeometric sampling identities are established; the contribution is their careful task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: Can establish a reusable foundation for checking diagnostic reliability before committing scarce budget to training interventions.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic fault coverage does not establish sensitivity to natural recommendation errors, diagnostic predictive value or validation HR@10 gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no retraining, extra checkpoint or production architecture change; frozen-score sampling checks mostly run on CPU.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent reference implementations, genuine future-dependent hooks, complete buffer and RNG restoration, loader isolation and noncircular fault accounting make integration substantially harder than the previous rating of four.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural basis for causal-prefix assertions and explicit residual-mapping checks.
limitations: Architectural reachability does not show which histories a fitted model uses.
Does not validate the proposed mutation suite or establish causal user intent.

related_work.title: An empirical study on metamorphic testing for recommender systems
contributions: Chengying Mao, Jifu Chen, Xiaorong Yi and Linlin Wen study six metamorphic relations across LibRec, PREA and Surprise.
Supports evaluating recommender implementations through expected output relationships.
limitations: Does not establish validity of the proposed NextItNet-specific relations or mutation operators.

related_work.title: Assessing the strength of Metamorphic Testing applied to optimisation software—Experience from industry
contributions: Alejandra Duque-Torres, Claus Klammer, Stefan Fischer, Dietmar Pfahl and Rudolf Ramler evaluate metamorphic testing using mutations of an industrial optimisation algorithm.
Its varied input-dependent mutation outcomes motivate reporting applicability, activation and survival separately.
limitations: This is an optimisation-software study, correcting the earlier report's recommender-study attribution.
Unchanged behavior on sampled inputs does not prove semantic equivalence.
Does not establish the proposed held-out operator-family protocol.

related_work.title: Activation-patching interpretation guidance (2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Provides methodological guidance on how intervention design, location and evaluation metrics affect activation-patching interpretation.
limitations: Does not supply a validated NextItNet-specific protocol or establish causal user intent.

related_work.title: SciPy documentation: scipy.stats.hypergeom
contributions: Defines the hypergeometric distribution for sampling without replacement.
Supports exact conditional expectations for sampled positive rank and HR@10 given frozen full-pool scores and a fixed tie order.
limitations: Requires unique uniform negative sampling from the declared eligible pool.
Sampling-law agreement does not establish recommendation relevance or preservation of full-catalog model ordering.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Krichene and Rendle show that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons, including in expectation.
Discusses bias and variance considerations for correction.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned benchmark or treating analytically calibrated sampled HR@10 as full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: Module
contributions: Documents forward hooks, module training modes and registered buffers.
Supports explicit handle removal and preservation of nonpersistent buffers.
limitations: Hook registration and state_dict use alone do not guarantee complete experimental-state restoration.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: DataLoader
contributions: Documents loading, worker processes, sampling and randomness relevant to diagnostic isolation.
limitations: Restoring main-process RNG state cannot rewind worker execution, iterator progress or prefetched data.

related_work.title: PyTorch documentation: random
limitations: Separate generator objects and non-Torch RNGs require explicit handling.
